chunks: And the women of the city said: 'The wife of Al-Aziz is enticing her page for himself; indeed, she has captured him with love. We see her in clear error.'

key_terms.الْمَدِينَةِ: the city (specifically Memphis/Al-Fustat in this context)

ai.seo_question: Who were the women gossiping about Prophet Yusuf in the city?
ai.summary: This verse, often cited in Shia exegesis as the opening of the story of Yusuf (AS), establishes the social backdrop of the Egyptian court where the elite women, led by the wife of Al-Aziz, gossip about Yusuf's beauty and their own infatuation. It highlights the theme of 'shaghaf' (deep, consuming passion) as a trial of character, contrasting the women's superficial judgment with Yusuf's inner purity and divine protection. The narrative underscores the societal pressure on prophets and the virtue of patience amidst social scrutiny and desire.
